originalTitle: Ford raises guidance after Q2 earnings beat, says F-Series recovery is on track
summary: Ford cited operational improvements, resilient vehicle pricing and a high sales mix of profitable products for its performance and the improved guidance.
content:
DETROIT — Ford Motor raised its 2026 earnings forecast Tuesday after beating Wall Street's second-quarter earnings expectations despite reporting a decline in revenue that slightly missed estimates.

Ford shares rose nearly 7% in after-hours trading Tuesday.

Here's how the company performed in the second quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:

The Detroit automaker cited operational improvements, resilient vehicle pricing and a high sales mix of profitable products for its performance as well as the improved guidance.

Ford's raised guidance includes full-year adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $10 billion and $11 billion, up from $8.5 billion to $10.5 billion. It also raised its expectations for adjusted free cash flow to $6 billion to $7 billion, up from $5 billion to $6 billion.

The additional free cash flow includes an earlier-than-expected cash recovery of $500 million of a previously announced $1.3 billion anticipated tariff reimbursement, the company said.

The earnings raise was led by a $500 million expected improvement to its traditional Ford Blue business to between $5 billion and $5.5 billion. It also narrowed earnings of its fleet business to between $7 billion and $7.5 billion from a previous low range of $6.5 billion.

"We delivered another strong quarter and raised our full-year guidance, but the more important story is the growing evidence that Ford is becoming a more profitable, more disciplined and genuinely different company," Ford CEO Jim Farley said in a release.

Ford cut expected losses of its Model e electric vehicle business to about $4 billion, compared with previous expectations of losses between $4 billion and $4.5 billion, and said it also expected slightly better results for its credit arm.

Each of the automotive business groups reported lower revenue compared with what analysts were expecting. Ford's total revenue, which includes its financial arm, was down 4% during the second quarter compared to a year earlier to $48.3 billion.

Ford reported a net loss of $1.3 billion during the second quarter largely due to one-time special charges related to its previously announced pullback in all-electric vehicles. The $4.2 billion in charges included $3.6 billion in restructuring of its BlueOval SK joint venture battery plant with SK On and $500 million due to a canceled EV program.

That loss was wider than the $36 million net loss it reported during the second quarter of 2025.

Ford reconfirmed plans to deliver full-year material and warranty cost reductions of approximately $1 billion despite an influx of recent recalls for the automaker.

Ford Chief Financial Officer Sherry House said the automaker's recovery of F-Series pickup truck production will continue into the back half of the year, reconfirming a roughly $1 billion improvement compared with last year's reported impact.

The automaker has had production problems with its F-Series trucks since Novelis, an aluminum supplier that provides material for its large trucks and SUVs, had two fires that crippled production. It restarted impacted production last month at that New York facility.

"We're successfully navigating the Novelis aluminum supply recovery plan, and we remain confident in our net $1 billion EBIT improvement in 2026, heavily weighted to the second half of the year," House said during a media call.

Ford said Tuesday it expects to recover about $2.5 billion of its vehicle volume lost due to the fires, which was the low end of a range of up to $3 billion.

During the company's earnings call Tuesday, House said the recovery is on the lower end of its prior estimate due to the mix of vehicles expected to be produced this year.

Heading into Ford's earnings report, Jefferies upgraded Ford and General Motors' stocks to buy from hold. Analyst Philippe Houchois said Ford is on track to start building momentum again, with the second quarter set to mark a trough.

"We see Q2 as a low point for volume with post-Novelis production set to normalize up," Houchois wrote. "With US market conditions healthy, management could raise guidance at Q2."
chineseTitle: 福特在第二季度盈利超出预期后上调指引，表示 F 系列复苏已步入正轨
chineseSummary: 福特将其业绩和指引的改进归功于运营改进、有弹性的汽车定价以及盈利产品的高销售组合。
chineseContent:
底特律——尽管营收下降略低于预期，福特汽车公司周二上调了 2026 年盈利预期，超出了华尔街第二季度的盈利预期。

周二盘后交易中，福特股价上涨近 7%。

以下是该公司第二季度的表现，与伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 编制的平均预期相比：

这家底特律汽车制造商将其业绩以及改进的指引归功于运营改进、弹性汽车定价和盈利产品的高销售组合。

福特上调的指引包括全年调整后息税前利润从 85 亿美元升至 105 亿美元，从 85 亿美元升至 100 亿美元至 110 亿美元。它还将调整后自由现金流的预期从 50 亿美元至 60 亿美元上调至 60 亿美元至 70 亿美元。

该公司表示，额外的自由现金流包括提前宣布的 13 亿美元关税补偿中提前收​​回的 5 亿美元现金。

此次盈利增长的主要原因是其传统的福特蓝业务预计将增加 5 亿美元，达到 50 亿至 55 亿美元。它还将车队业务的盈利从之前的 65 亿美元的低点缩小至 70 亿至 75 亿美元。

福特首席执行官吉姆·法利（Jim Farley）在一份新闻稿中表示：“我们又实现了强劲的季度业绩，并提高了全年指引，但更重要的是，越来越多的证据表明，福特正在成为一家盈利能力更强、更有纪律、真正与众不同的公司。”

福特将其 Model e 电动汽车业务的预期损失削减至约 40 亿美元，而此前的预期损失为 40 亿至 45 亿美元，并表示预计其信贷部门的业绩将略有好转。

每个汽车业务集团的收入均低于分析师的预期。福特第二季度的总收入（包括其金融部门）较上年同期下降 4%，至 483 亿美元。

福特报告称，第二季度净亏损 13 亿美元，主要是由于其先前宣布的全电动汽车缩减计划而产生的一次性特殊费用。这 42 亿美元的费用包括 36 亿美元用于重组其与 SK On 的 BlueOval SK 合资电池工厂，以及因取消电动汽车项目而产生的 5 亿美元。

这一亏损比 2025 年第二季度报告的 3600 万美元净亏损还要大。

尽管最近汽车制造商大量召回，但福特仍重申计划将全年材料和保修成本削减约 10 亿美元。

福特首席财务官 Sherry House 表示，该汽车制造商 F 系列皮卡生产的复苏将持续到今年下半年，再次证实与去年报告的影响相比，产量增加了约 10 亿美元。

自从为其大型卡车和 SUV 提供材料的铝供应商诺贝丽斯发生两起火灾导致生产瘫痪以来，该汽车制造商的 F 系列卡车就出现了生产问题。纽约工厂上个月重新启动了受影响的生产。

豪斯在媒体电话会议上表示：“我们正在成功实施诺贝丽斯铝供应复苏计划，我们对 2026 年息税前利润净改善 10 亿美元仍然充满信心，尤其是下半年。”

福特周二表示，预计将挽回因火灾造成的车辆损失中约 25 亿美元，这是最高 30 亿美元损失范围的低端。

在周二的公司财报电话会议上，豪斯表示，由于今年预计生产的车辆数量较多，复苏程度低于之前预期。

在福特财报发布前，杰富瑞将福特和通用汽车的股票评级从持有上调至买入。分析师 Philippe Houchois 表示，福特有望再次开始建立动力，第二季度将迎来低谷。

Houchois 写道：“我们认为第二季度是销量的低点，诺贝丽斯之后的产量将恢复正常。” “由于美国市场状况健康，管理层可能会提高第二季度的指导。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
